units.passage: No. Sensitive, restricted or unpublished research data must not be entered into tools that have not been approved for that data type. units.passage: As with any other platform or tool, any data used with Generative AI tools must be securely stored and handled according to the UA’s data handling policies. units.passage: Avoid sharing information that is legally or confidentially restricted.

units.why: 'Any data you enter into a Generative AI tool becomes part of its training data' states a fact about data retention and exposure; it is the P50 rationale (tools store prompts), informs.

units.passage: When using Gen AI technology individuals should not enter Category 1 or Category 2 data , including non-public research data into Gen AI tools of which the university has not entered into a contract with.
units.policy: Individuals should not enter Category 1 or Category 2 data, including non-public research data, into Gen AI tools with which the university has no contract.
units.why: "individuals should not enter Category 1 or Category 2 data" into tools without a university contract is a data-protection prohibition addressed to everyone, so P50 (protect data, prefer contracted tools), should-not as worded.

units.passage: Information shared with Gen AI is not private and could expose proprietary or sensitive information to unauthorized parties. Information provided in prompts to Gen AI is often stored by the AI software to be used in future outputs and to train or re-train future Gen AI models.
units.why: "Information shared with Gen AI is not private" and prompts are stored to train models explains why the data rule exists; a factual warning about tool data practices, so P50 with informs.

units.passage: Shared both the faculty members’ data and the data of students
units.why: "Shared both the faculty members’ data and the data of students" names a data-sharing risk of detection tools; the specific concern is data protection, so P50 rather than P39.

units.passage: These include, but are not limited to, ensuring protection of confidential, personal, or business information and intellectual property,
units.why: "ensuring protection of confidential, personal, or business information and intellectual property" names data and IP protection as a duty when using AI. P50 (protect personal data) fits best; IP is only mentioned in passing and is not a licensing rule (P52).

units.passage: Unless you are using a GenAI application that ensures separation of your entry from other entries and confidentiality (usually a paid service), uploading content into GenAI (Open GenAI) is a public disclosure.
units.why: "uploading content into GenAI (Open GenAI) is a public disclosure" is a factual warning about data exposure. P50 (protect data; tools store prompts) fits since it explains why privacy matters; modality informs.

units.passage: It is safest to assume data or queries uploaded into Open GenAI tools will become public information,
units.why: "It is safest to assume data or queries uploaded into Open GenAI tools will become public information" is advice to assume exposure. It is a recommendation (should) about data protection, P50.

units.passage: In order to protect Caltech data and information, do not enter, contribute, or otherwise input sensitive, confidential, or restricted information into Open GenAI tools.
units.why: "do not enter ... sensitive, confidential, or restricted information into Open GenAI tools" is a prohibition for all users on a specific kind of input. P50 fits (protect confidential data); P20 covers assignment specs and student code, which this is not.

units.passage: This includes, but is not limited to, data covered by regulations such as FERPA and HIPAA, any intellectual property or unpublished research data, export-controlled data, and other sensitive HR, business, or administrative data.
units.why: The list "data covered by regulations such as FERPA and HIPAA ... export-controlled data" defines what counts as restricted data and so sets the scope of the prohibition above. P50 again, as a definition of protected categories; informs.

units.passage: Review and make some recommendations on the use of specific GAI technologies at Cal Poly (e.g., ChatGPT.edu).
units.why: "Review and make some recommendations on the use of specific GAI technologies at Cal Poly (e.g., ChatGPT.edu)" concerns which tools are vetted for campus use (P50).

units.passage: Anything that is uploaded to a publicly available AI tool effectively enters the public domain.
units.why: Principle 3 states "Anything that is uploaded to a publicly available AI tool effectively enters the public domain", a privacy fact motivating data protection, so P50 as informs.

units.passage: Generative AI tools which have not passed a campus security review may be used with public data only.
units.why: "Generative AI tools which have not passed a campus security review may be used with public data only" limits unvetted tools to public data, so P50 (vetted tools, protect data); restrictive in effect.
units.fit_note: Also functions as a campus security review requirement (P65) for any tool used with non-public data.

units.passage: Adhering to AI security and privacy practices is vital to protecting UCR’s intellectual property and individual user data.
units.why: The instructor practice "Adhering to AI security and privacy practices is vital to protecting UCR's intellectual property and individual user data" tells instructors to protect data, P50.

units.passage: Always ensure that the software or platform you're using is from a reputable source and has adequate security measures.
units.why: "Always ensure that the software or platform you're using is from a reputable source and has adequate security measures" tells students to prefer vetted tools, P50.

units.passage: Avoid sharing personal or sensitive information.
units.why: "Avoid sharing personal or sensitive information" protects personal data when using AI, P50.

units.passage: Additionally, be wary of freely available online AI tools that may not have clearly stated privacy policies or may use your data for undisclosed purposes.
units.why: "be wary of freely available online AI tools that may not have clearly stated privacy policies" cautions about unvetted tools, P50.

units.passage: However, individual responsibility plays a significant role in maintaining this safety net.
units.why: "individual responsibility plays a significant role in maintaining this safety net" places part of data protection on the student, P50.

units.passage: Also think about privacy (what info do students have to share?), security (what info is the intelligence accessing?) and equity (do all students have access?) issues if you decide to remote proctor or require the use of any artificial intelligence tools in your class.
units.why: "Also think about privacy (what info do students have to share?), security (what info is the intelligence accessing?)" tells instructors to weigh privacy and security when they require AI tools or remote proctoring, so P50.

units.passage: Gen AI platforms like ChatGPT are trained on pre-existing data sets, but they also use the content that we put into them to train the models.
units.why: The page says Gen AI platforms "use the content that we put into them to train the models". This warns about data use, P50.

units.passage: If you do not wish for your content to be included in the training data, here are ways you can change this setting for various AI models.
units.why: "If you do not wish for your content to be included in the training data, here are ways you can change this setting" points users to privacy settings, P50.

units.passage: You should not input or share personal, confidential, sensitive data, or intellectual property when using AI tools.
units.why: "You should not input or share personal, confidential, sensitive data, or intellectual property" is a privacy rule for AI tools, P50.
